title: Michigan Energy Assistance Program 2026-27: What It Covers
desc: Michigan's MEAP helps low-income households pay electric, gas, propane and heating oil bills. Funding is $1.50 per meter a month. Read what the state says.
h1: Michigan Heating Help 2026-27: Michigan Energy Assistance Program
lead: Michigan's Energy Assistance Program, called MEAP, helps low-income households pay their home energy bills. This page sticks to what the Michigan Public Service Commission page says. It does not give household dates or dollar benefits, so we do not show any.
cards_heading: What we found for Michigan heating help
cards_intro: Each card names the official page we read on October 21, 2026. Dollar amounts are the state's own; anything it does not publish, we do not show.

cards.title: MEAP bill help
cards.note: Payment or partial payment of bills for electricity, natural gas, propane, heating oil or another deliverable heating fuel at your main home.

sections: The program helps eligible low-income households meet home energy costs at their primary residence. It can pay all or part of bills for electricity, natural gas, propane, heating oil and other deliverable fuels used for heat. By law it must put vulnerable people first and, where it fits, add services that help households move toward self-sufficiency.

MEAP is paid for by a charge on electric bills called the Low-Income Energy Assistance Funding Factor. On April 17, 2026 the Michigan Public Service Commission set it at $1.50 per meter per month for the electric utilities that choose to take part, starting with the September 2026 billing month.

For fiscal year 2027 the commission asked nonprofits, local governments and tribal governments to apply for grants. The page lists an estimated $93,000,000 in total program funding. Those grants go to the local providers that serve households, so you do not apply to the commission.

The page points to a Get Help link. In practice you reach a local provider, and the provider decides if you qualify and how much you get. We did not find an income table or a dollar benefit on the page we read, so we are not guessing. Call 211 or use the Get Help link for your county.
The state also runs other help that lives on different pages, such as emergency relief for utility bills. We did not verify them on official pages today, so we leave them off until we can read them.
Use rebates to cut the bill
Bill help is a short-term bridge. For lasting savings, look at the Michigan rebate pages below.

Because MEAP is paid by a charge on electric bills, it is tied to utilities that choose to take part. The state page names a funding factor for participating electric utilities. If you are not sure whether your electric company takes part, ask the provider you reach through the Get Help link. We did not find a list of participating utilities on the page we read, so we do not name any.
Using the page with a neighbour

Many people who need help do not use the internet. If you are helping a parent or a neighbour, call 211 with them and help them write down the provider's name and phone number. Ask what documents are needed and when to call back. A short list on paper makes the second call much easier.

When the commission or a provider publishes a household income table or a benefit schedule for 2026-27, we will read it on the official page and add it with the date. Until then, this page stays short on purpose.
claim_heading: What to do in Michigan this winter
claim_steps: Use the Get Help link on the Michigan PSC page to find your provider.
Ask the provider for the income limit and the benefit for your fuel.
Have recent bills and proof of income ready.
Ask about weatherization or services that lower the bill later.
Look at efficiency rebates for next winter.
